checks.claim_checked: Walsh signs, normalization, three example amplitudes, projection check
checks.reason: Exact rational amplitudes are 1, 0, -1 and 1/2; projection probabilities are their squares.

checks.claim_checked: 180-gate circuit, named gate example, 371 local tests
checks.reason: All 256 input assignments match the rational promise predicate. The gate example and local-test count agree.

checks.claim_checked: Base and domain-board truth values, failed output tests
checks.reason: All 16 candidate pairs checked per board; unique base winner and domain-board rejection agree.

checks.claim_checked: Repetition error and all-input cap
checks.reason: Both Chernoff tails are at most exp(-rho*c/16); the ceiling and integer threshold are safe. Fresh retained registers preserve the trial law.

checks.claim_checked: Circuit promise test, size, and actual bit-length estimate
checks.reason: Integer threshold equivalence and the linked gate-count derivation support the stated size. The total input has O_k(m^22 log^3 m) bits.

checks.claim_checked: Complementarity, off-promise rival dominance, cycle and false-pointer changes
checks.reason: Canonical pair ordering establishes complementary laws; an all-one genuine winner is never disqualified by a rival pointer. Both mutations have the printed behavior.

checks.claim_checked: Expected halving and missing-winner probability
checks.reason: Pairing complementary probabilities gives exact drift. Missing the winner implies its weight remains above 1/2; absorption cannot occur before it is listed.

checks.claim_checked: Fresh-register product law and fractional sampling
checks.reason: Conditional on fixed input, history and label, separate workspaces multiply success probabilities. Orthogonal labels add masses. Fractional values agree exactly.

checks.claim_checked: Grover rotation, successful-label preservation, bounded randomized retries
checks.reason: The printed matrices have correct signs. The bounded schedule has a 9/40 success floor in its guaranteed range and an all-input cap; mixing identical successful laws causes no bias.

checks.claim_checked: Coupling, stopping, retained winner, verification polarity and errors
checks.reason: Only failures before the winner is listed matter; union bound adds T*epsilon. Nonwinners fail a test at every address. One- and zero-input error accounts are correctly separated.

checks.claim_checked: Quantum all-branch query count and logarithmic power six
checks.reason: Tournament and verification add. The intentionally loose replacements yield the printed sixth- and fifth-power costs.

checks.claim_checked: Common minimax law, planted pair, first-difference coupling
checks.reason: Finite separation yields one law for all capped trees. Dummy zero and planted one inputs differ only at the two stated locations. Overcounting true-cell visits is safe.

checks.claim_checked: Erased-zero identity, posterior uniformity, early/late bound
checks.reason: Independence from the whole dummy run yields E[Z]/m. Transcript constraints preserve unread-row uniformity. Early/late discovery costs give 4G/m^2.

checks.claim_checked: Whole-run lightness and stopped predictor
checks.reason: The predictor has total target cap L on every tuple, hence separate cap L. Light visit is contained in predictor success; default success prevents equality. No conditioning on compliance is used.

checks.claim_checked: XOR trace and modified exercise
checks.reason: Enumeration gives 1/8 joint visit, 1/4 predictor success, and 1/8 at each fixed time in the stopping modification. A later target read removes the cheap branch from whole-run lightness.

checks.claim_checked: Direct-product hypotheses and proof; column averaging
checks.reason: Compatible transcripts factor; one continuation factor changes per query. Separate caps and joint independence are used at the required steps. Averaging over I cancels the m column factor.

checks.claim_checked: Tail, discrepancy, floors, fixed-parameter ratio
checks.reason: r=40t gives beta^r <= m^-10; the discrepancy is below 1/3. Integrality gives R>mL/100 directly. Positive exponent d yields divergence after fixing k.

checks.claim_checked: Endpoint and formal statement strength
checks.reason: The compared family has existential log power and a floor lower bound; named-circuit source supplies six and 1/400 on the same function. Growing-k refinement is correctly separated.

checks.claim_checked: n=0 exposition versus n>=1 formal convention
checks.reason: Every length-zero total Boolean function is constant and has R=Q=0. Adding it changes no admissible universal exponent.

checks.claim_checked: Exact Forrelation supplier statement and eventual floor consequence
checks.reason: Supplied PDF printed page 4 confirms Theorem 1.3/Corollary 1.4 and one-sided threshold. Fixed-k ratio grows as log(m)^(1+1/k). The whole analytic proof was not re-audited.
